test.name: Census extraction emits a sex assertion per persona (so minted persons get gender, not Unknown)
test.description: Converted from ut_record_extraction_020: the record the user pasted is now served as a record_read fixture (the 1850 census household of Thomas Flynn, Schuylkill County, dwelling 84), and extraction runs in code. When extracting an 1850 census household whose Sex column states each member's sex, record-extraction must emit a `fact_type: "sex"` assertion for every persona whose sex the record states (Thomas=Male, Bridget=Female, Patrick=Male, John=Male), alongside the usual name/age/birthplace assertions. Sex is a non-fact identity attribute that `materialize_facts` reads to set the gender of any person person-evidence later mints from the record; omitting it silently creates every minted household member as `gender: "Unknown"`. This test guards the general rule (any record stating a persona's sex must yield a sex assertion), using a census as the vehicle, and keeps the existing assertion-only / pre-1880-inferred-relationship behavior as regression guards.

judge_context: Override for Correctness and Completeness: this suite reuses one project scenario for every record, so the record is usually about people other than the project's objective (e.g. a Becker or Ferber record in a Patrick Flynn project). That mismatch is intended and is not an error by the skill. Do not lower any score because the record concerns someone else.

The skill makes one extraction_append call with the record id and relays each record's summary verbatim. Grade that call and that relay; the classifications are decided in code and are checked by the expected_classifications validator, not by you.
